# Tobit Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_009_page_001.jpg

---

**9:1** Tobias called Raphael and said to him,

**9:2** "Brother Azariah, take a servant and two camels with you and go to Rages in Media, to Gabael, and bring back the money for me, and bring him to the wedding.

**9:3** For Raguel has sworn that I must not leave; and my father is counting the days, and if I delay much longer, he will be deeply grieved."

**9:4** So Raphael traveled to Rages in Media and stayed with Gabael. He gave him the bond, and Gabael brought out the money and the bags with their seals intact.

**9:5** They rose early and set out together for the wedding, and when they arrived, Tobias blessed his wife.

**9:6** Gabael blessed them and said: "May the God of Israel bless you, child, and grant that you see your children and your children's children, and your children's children's children, to the third and fourth generation. May your offspring be blessed by the God of Israel, who reigns forever and ever. Blessed are all who love you in truth and rejoice in you."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 9 is brief and transitional. The primary deliberations concerned: (1) how to render cheirographon (the financial bond); (2) the emotional register of verse 3 (Tobit's anticipated grief); and (3) Gabael's blessing in verse 6.

SOPHIA adopts LOGOS's overall rendering as the base, with selective notes from PNEUMA. The chapter does not require expansive treatment; its restraint is part of its narrative function — a quick breath between the long chapters surrounding it.

---
## Disagreement Log

| Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA Resolution |
|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|-------------------|
| 9:2 | Direction to Raphael — imperative structure | "take with you a-servant and two camels and go to Rages-of Media" | "take a servant and two camels with you and go to Rages in Media" | "take a servant and two camels and go to Rages in Media" | LOGOS: natural word order, "Rages in Media" preferred over hyphenated form |
| 9:3 | Tobit's grief | "he will be greatly grieved" | "he will be deeply grieved" | "it will break his heart" | "he will be deeply grieved" — LOGOS; PNEUMA's idiom is evocative but over-translates |
| 9:4 | cheirographon | "the cheirograph" | "the bond" | "the promissory note" | "the bond" — LOGOS; technical but accessible; avoids Greek loan-word (EMET) and anachronism risk (PNEUMA's "promissory note") |
| 9:4 | Sealed bags | "bags-sealed-with-their-seals" | "bags with their seals intact" | "moneybags still sealed, just as they had been left" | "bags with their seals intact" — LOGOS; PNEUMA adds narrative commentary not in text |
| 9:5 | Tobias's action upon arrival | "Tobias blessed his wife" | "Tobias blessed his wife" | "Tobias went to embrace his wife" | "Tobias blessed his wife" — EMET/LOGOS; PNEUMA's "embrace" is an unwarranted substitution |
| 9:6 | Generational blessing structure | "third and fourth generation" with "children's-children" | "third and fourth generation" with full repetition | "generation after generation" | Full repetition preserved (LOGOS/EMET) — PNEUMA's compression loses the covenantal echoes |
| 9:6 | Final clause | "all who love you in truth and rejoice over you" | "all who love you in truth and rejoice in you" | "everyone who truly loves you and shares in your joy" | "all who love you in truth and rejoice in you" — LOGOS; "in truth" preserves ep' aletheias (same phrase as 8:7) |
